title: Overloading ambiguity and maintenance risk
answer: Overloading becomes error-prone when several overloads accept unrelated reference types or when boxing, varargs, and null are mixed so that a call is ambiguous or selects a less obvious candidate. For example, `process(String)` and `process(Integer)` make `process(null)` ambiguous because neither parameter type is more specific than the other. Good APIs keep overload sets small, predictable, and semantically consistent.
